domains.description: Domains the carrier sends mail from or hosts tracking pages on.

items.description: A mail or web domain; subdomains match too.

courier_codes.description: courier_code values of tracking-number files whose formats belong to this carrier (the carrier's own id is implied).

upu_countries.description: Countries whose UPU S10 numbers (e.g. RR123456785DE) this carrier delivers.

tracking_urls.description: Tracking page templates keyed by locale ('default', a language such as 'de', or a full tag such as 'de-AT' for a regional site). {tracking_number} is replaced by the URL-encoded number; any other {name} (lower-case, e.g. {postcode}) by the value the caller passes, and a template whose placeholders are not all given is skipped.

tracking_number_pattern.description: Shape of a number the carrier's own tracker accepts, anchored with ^ and $: a plausibility check before a lookup is sent, not detection (see tracking-numbers).

pattern.description: A regex in the portable subset.

crossref.description: Identifiers of this carrier in other systems, e.g. 17track: '100001'.

regex.description: Whitespace-tolerant pattern; an array is joined into one pattern. Named groups SerialNumber and CheckDigit feed the checksum.

exists.description: Names of `additional` lookups that must find a row for the number to be valid.

items.description: One row of an additional lookup: `matches` (exact) or `matches_regex` (whole value), plus descriptive string fields such as name, description, country or courier.

code_prefix.description: The code starts with this text (compared ignoring case). Tried after exact codes, in file order.

text.description: Regex searched in the status text.

fields.description: Only when every listed raw field also equals its value, e.g. { lang: fr } for a sentence that exists in one page language only.

propertyNames.description: Name of a raw status field, as the carrier's payload calls it.
Name of a raw status field, as the carrier's payload calls it.

fields.description: Every listed field of the raw status equals its value (both trimmed, case kept). Tried before codes and texts, in file order, so list the most specific entry first.

status.description: Canonical parcel status. at_pickup_point means arrived and waiting for collection; a parcel still on its way to a pickup point is in_transit with pickup: true.

pickup.description: The parcel is going to, or waiting at, a pickup point or locker.

confirmed.description: false marks a plausible guess not yet seen in real data. Defaults to true.

label.description: A neutral English display text for the raw value, for carriers whose own wording can carry personal data (a shop name, an address).

stage.description: Order of this step in the carrier's journey (higher is later), for consumers that must order events with the same time. Only meaningful within one table.

entries.description: Field entries are tried first, then exact codes, then code prefixes, then texts; within each kind the first hit in file order wins.

ignore.description: Values that say the item is no parcel at all (a cancelled or refunded order line). Matched like entries, but kept apart from them: mapping never returns these.

code_prefix.description: The code starts with this text (compared ignoring case). Tried after exact codes, in file order.

text.description: Regex searched in the status text.

fields.description: Only when every listed raw field also equals its value, e.g. { lang: fr } for a sentence that exists in one page language only.

propertyNames.description: Name of a raw status field, as the carrier's payload calls it.
Name of a raw status field, as the carrier's payload calls it.

fields.description: Every listed field of the raw status equals its value (both trimmed, case kept). Tried before codes and texts, in file order, so list the most specific entry first.

event.description: What the value says instead of a parcel status, e.g. order_cancelled.

months.description: Twelve lists (January first) of month names and abbreviations.

weekdays.description: Seven lists (Monday first) of weekday names. Keep risky short forms out (German 'so', 'do').

relative_days.description: Words for a day relative to today, e.g. tomorrow: 1.

past_days.description: Words that name today or a past day on their own, as timeline headers and delivered lines use them (today: 0, yesterday: -1). Not used by the arrival parser.

lead_ins.description: Words that announce an arrival. A bare relative day or weekday only counts after one.

range_separators.description: Words that join the two ends of a range (dashes are always accepted).

window_openers.description: Words that may open a time window, e.g. between, zwischen.

deadline_words.description: Words before a single time meaning 'at the latest', e.g. by, bis.

point_words.description: Words before a single time meaning 'at', e.g. um, at.

hour_words.description: Words after a time that mark it as a clock time, e.g. uhr, o'clock.

pattern.description: A regex in the portable subset.

anyOf.description: A regex in the portable subset (no lookaround, backreferences, atomic groups, possessive quantifiers, \A/\Z or inline flags; named groups as (?<name>...)).

negatives.description: If any matches (case-insensitively), the text announces no arrival at all.

pattern.description: A regex in the portable subset.

anyOf.description: A regex in the portable subset (no lookaround, backreferences, atomic groups, possessive quantifiers, \A/\Z or inline flags; named groups as (?<name>...)).

cut_markers.description: Text from the first match onwards is ignored (e.g. 'previously expected ...').

tracking_keywords.description: Words that introduce a tracking number in prose; used by the mail fallback detector.

local_parts.description: If set, a sender matched by `domains` must also have one of these local parts (e.g. shipment-tracking for shipment-tracking@amazon.de). Compared case-insensitively.

flags.description: Flags for every bare-string pattern in this rule.

subject.description: If set, at least one must match the subject.

pattern.description: A regex in the portable subset.

anyOf.description: A regex in the portable subset (no lookaround, backreferences, atomic groups, possessive quantifiers, \A/\Z or inline flags; named groups as (?<name>...)).

exclude.description: If any matches the subject, the rule does not apply.

pattern.description: A regex in the portable subset.

anyOf.description: A regex in the portable subset (no lookaround, backreferences, atomic groups, possessive quantifiers, \A/\Z or inline flags; named groups as (?<name>...)).

body.description: If set, at least one must match the text (or the HTML as text); for senders such as marketplaces that relay emails of several carriers.

anyOf.description: A regex in the portable subset (no lookaround, backreferences, atomic groups, possessive quantifiers, \A/\Z or inline flags; named groups as (?<name>...)).

pattern.description: Must contain a named group called like the field, e.g. (?<tracking_number>...).

in.description: Where to search; html means the HTML part converted to plain text.

status_keywords.description: Checked in order; the first group with a matching pattern sets the status.

status.description: Canonical parcel status. at_pickup_point means arrived and waiting for collection; a parcel still on its way to a pickup point is in_transit with pickup: true.

anyOf.description: A regex in the portable subset (no lookaround, backreferences, atomic groups, possessive quantifiers, \A/\Z or inline flags; named groups as (?<name>...)).

default_status.description: Canonical parcel status. at_pickup_point means arrived and waiting for collection; a parcel still on its way to a pickup point is in_transit with pickup: true.

carrier.description: The carrier when the mail names none (see carrier_from).

carrier_from.description: Take the carrier from the extracted carrier field, normalised via carriers.yaml aliases; falls back to `carrier`.

extractors.description: Named code extractors (src/mail/extractors) for what a regex cannot express.

require.description: Fields that must be found for the rule to produce a result.

name.description: What the consumer asks for, unique per carrier, e.g. api_key.

purpose.description: Where the carrier expects the value and why.

source.description: Where the value was read from: the public website or the carrier's app.

last_verified.description: Date the value was last seen working.
